added_claim_errors: 'United's travel credits are typically valid for one year from issuance': United policy the answer could not have checked, and it contradicts the DOT rule that a credit offered instead of a refund must stay valid for at least 5 years
'that's a reasonable and standard request' (the one-year ask): wrong, because the law requires at least 5 years, so one year is asking for less than the person is owed

'Weather affects what the airline owes you in compensation': misleading, since US law gives no EU261-style cash compensation for cancellations; weather affects only airlines' voluntary meal and hotel commitments

reasons: A corrects the agent's wrong premise in its first line and links to the DOT refunds page, which can be checked. Its weak point is that it still drafts a message accepting the credit, and that message openly gives up the refund. It also misses the 5-year minimum and the 7-business-day deadline. B drafts the same acceptance message and only corrects the premise at the end. It then calls one year 'reasonable and standard', citing United's credit policy without having checked it, which contradicts the 5-year rule. B also hints at weather-related 'compensation' that US law does not provide. Neither answer drafts the refund request the key asks for, but A handles the trap earlier and adds no false claims, so A wins.
